root_cause.text: In AppArmor's aa_replace_profiles(), ownership of the dynamically allocated ent->ns_name string was transferred to the local ns_name pointer without clearing ent->ns_name, leaving two cleanup paths to free the same allocation.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `ent->ns_name = NULL;` immediately after `ns_name = ent->ns_name;`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that `aa_load_ent_free(ent)` frees `ent->ns_name` and later `kfree(ns_name)` frees it again, causing a double free.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the relevant ownership transfer and cleanup paths inside aa_replace_profiles(). The vulnerable construct is present in the new namespace consistency loop: `else if (ent->ns_name) { ... ns_name = ent->ns_name; }`. This assigns the dynamically allocated `ent->ns_name` to the local `ns_name` pointer, effectively transferring ownership, but the code does not clear `ent->ns_name` afterward. Later, on the failure/cleanup path, the function audits using `ns_name` at label `fail:` via `audit_policy(..., ns_name, ...)`, and then frees all load entries with `list_for_each_entry_safe(ent, tmp, &lh, list) { ... aa_load_ent_free(ent); }`. Since `aa_load_ent_free(ent)` will free `ent->ns_name`, while `ns_name` still aliases the same allocation and is also treated as a separately owned object in the function's cleanup design, this is exactly the double-free/duplicate-ownership root cause described. There is no statement such as `ent->ns_name = NULL;` after `ns_name = ent->ns_name;`, so the fix is not present.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet includes the full body of `aa_replace_profiles()` and shows the relevant ownership/cleanup paths, so it is sufficient. The vulnerable construct is present because `aa_unpack(udata, size, &lh, &ns_name);` returns both a separate `ns_name` pointer and a load-entry list `lh`. On failure or at function exit, the code frees the entries via `aa_load_ent_free(ent)` in both the success loop and the `fail:` cleanup loop, while also separately dropping the namespace prepared from `ns_name` via `aa_put_namespace(ns)`. The root-cause described is that ownership of `ent->ns_name` was transferred to local `ns_name` without clearing `ent->ns_name`, creating two frees of the same allocation through the local path and entry cleanup path. This commit shows the new multi-entry logic introducing `struct aa_load_ent *ent, *tmp;`, `LIST_HEAD(lh);`, `error = aa_unpack(udata, size, &lh, &ns_name);`, and later `aa_load_ent_free(ent);` / cleanup of all entries, but there is no code clearing any entry-owned `ns_name` after transfer. There is also no defensive handling such as `ent->ns_name = NULL` or equivalent after unpack/transfer. Therefore the bug is present and the fix is not yet included.
